title: introduce-sliding-window-drift-smoke-eval-hook-with-weighted-stability-score
author: Nora Kaplan
description:
Summary: Adds a new CI hook and eval primitive that runs a time-windowed (sliding-window) smoke evaluation across prompt cohorts to detect short-term drift and flaky regressions. The hook computes per-cohort percentile delta metrics over recent windows, applies a configurable decay-weighted stability score, and fails the CI gate when a stability budget is exceeded. Motivation: existing cohort/threshold checks are effective for steady regressions but noisy for short bursts and time-localized drift. This PR implements a sliding-window approach to reduce noise, surface sustained degradations faster, and avoid false positives from transient spikes. The change is intended for use as a pre-merge smoke gate in fast-moving model rollouts and nightly regression sweeps.

What I changed (single continuous description): Added a new hook class SlidingWindowDriftHook that samples recent evaluation runs and computes per-cohort windowed deltas (window_size and step configurable). Introduced a StabilityScorer that applies exponential decay to older windows and aggregates a weighted percentile delta (default: 75th percentile) across cohorts. Implemented an optional alignment mode that matches window boundaries across cohorts with sparse data, and a fallback sampling strategy when a cohort lacks recent examples. Added a CLI flag (--sliding-window-config) to the eval runner and a new YAML example in examples/hooks/sliding-window.yaml. Wired the hook into CI via eval-ci-adapter so it can emit a single pass/fail result plus a compact JSON summary artifact for the CI job UI.

Files changed (high-level):
- eval_harness/hooks/sliding_window_drift.py: new hook implementation, core algorithm and config parsing
- eval_harness/scoring/stability.py: new StabilityScorer module and unit tests
- eval_harness/cli/run_eval.py: CLI flag parsing and result artifact emission
- examples/hooks/sliding-window.yaml: example config and thresholds
- tests/unit/test_sliding_window.py: unit tests for window math, decay and percentile aggregation
- tests/integration/test_ci_integration.py: integration test that runs the hook against synthetic time-series data
- docs/ops/ci-hooks.md: documentation explaining tuning knobs and recommended thresholds for smoke gates

Commits (summary):
- 7c9d3a4: add sliding window hook and basic tests
- a1bfe21: add stability scorer + percentile aggregator
- c5d2f88: CLI wiring, artifact emission, and example config
- e0f7b11: integration test and synthetic datasets
- f3a92d0: docs and small refactor based on review feedback

Testing and CI: Tests added include deterministic unit tests for window alignment and decay math, and an integration harness that simulates a 14-day time series with injected transient spikes and a slow drift to validate both sensitivity and false-positive rate. CI ran full unit and integration matrix on py38/py39 and passed. A rerun was required after a transient flake in the integration matrix; final CI status: pass. The CI job emits a compact JSON artifact (sliding-window-summary.json) that CI dashboards can display; example artifact is included in test fixtures.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Jamal: "Nice approach — can we make the default decay half-life configurable and documented? Also request to surface per-cohort sample counts in the artifact so SREs can triage." — addressed in commit f3a92d0.
- Eleni: "Can the scorer be pluggable so future metrics (e.g., response-time percentiles) can reuse it?" — refactored stability.py to expose a small public API for pluggable metrics.
- Priya: "Please add a note in docs about expected false-positive behavior for small cohorts and recommended guardrails." — added to docs/ops/ci-hooks.md.
- Jamal: "Approve after tests and docs." — Approved.

Merge outcome: merged to main via squash merge. Squash commit message: "sliding window drift smoke eval hook: add hook, scorer, tests, CI integration, docs". Merge performed by Jamal Ortiz after approvals and CI green.

Usage notes and rollout: The hook is off by default. Teams can enable it on specific repos or branches by adding the provided YAML and connecting the eval-ci-adapter. Recommended initial config: window_size=7 (days), step=1 (day), decay_half_life=3 (days), percentile=75, min_samples_per_cohort=50. For small cohorts enable alignment_mode: "sparse".

Related work: complements cohort-aware changepoint detectors and the recent historical-variance detector; this hook is optimized for rapid pre-merge smoke gating where speedy detection of short-lived regressions matters. Linear refs: ENG-2024 (sliding-window design) and ENG-2138 (CI adapter integration).
release_notes: New CI hook: sliding-window drift smoke eval. Allows teams to detect short-lived regressions with a decay-weighted stability score and emit CI artifacts for triage. Off by default; docs include tuning guidance.
notes_for_qa: Run tests/unit/test_sliding_window.py and tests/integration/test_ci_integration.py. Use the provided synthetic fixture to validate both sensitivity and false positive rate. Verify sliding-window-summary.json artifact structure in CI job artifacts.
